entry.title: Task Manager Pause Button 1.0.0
entry.content:
Task Manager Pause Button

Add a native Pause / Resume button next to Run new task in the Windows 11 Task Manager on the Processes and Details pages.

How to use

  1. Open Task Manager and select Processes or Details.
  2. Click Pause to stop the list from updating.
  3. Click Resume to start updating again.

The button controls Task Manager's refresh hold on Processes and Details. The mod does not suspend apps, stop Windows processes, or change the Real time update speed setting.

Compatibility and limitations

  • Works with the Windows 11 Task Manager XAML interface. Windows updates may change private Task Manager functions or controls.
  • Uses Task Manager's Ctrl-key refresh hold through GetKeyState calls made directly by Taskmgr.exe. While paused, some Task Manager keyboard actions may behave as if Ctrl is held, including Run new task (Ctrl+click can open Command Prompt instead of the normal dialog). This does not affect other apps.
  • Recognizes the tested Task Manager command-bar layout independently of display language: one command bar with four native buttons, with Run new task in the first position. Falls back to English/Portuguese labels or recognizable control identifiers on other layouts. Other Windows versions can have different layouts, so all languages/builds are not guaranteed.
  • Pause/Resume labels are in English regardless of the Task Manager language.
  • Keeps Pause active when moving between Processes and Details. Automatically resumes when navigating to another page if the navigation-exit symbol is available on your Windows build.
  • If the button is missing, close and reopen Task Manager with the mod enabled.
  • No settings or background applications are needed.

Source and feedback

GitHub

Author: Luiz Bizzio. License: Apache-2.0.

entry.title: Quick Look 1.0.0
entry.content:
Quick Look

A native Quick Look preview for Windows File Explorer, packed as a Windhawk mod.

Select a file or a folder and press Space. That is the whole idea.

Quick Look docks a real panel inside the File Explorer window, next to the file list, and previews whatever is selected. It is not a floating window: it is a child of the Explorer tab, so it moves with it, is clipped to it and, if you want, shrinks the Details columns to reserve its own space, the way File Pilot's inspector does.

Folders open with Explorer's own file list, not a copy: the same icons, columns, sorting, view modes and scrollbars. Text, images, video, audio, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, archives and everything else have their own preview or a proper fallback. Nothing runs on a timer in the background, and nothing that touches the disk ever blocks Explorer.

Highlights

  • A panel, not a window. Space opens it, Space or Esc closes it, the header has a close button for the mouse. It docks on the right, or at the bottom when the window is too narrow; drag its edge to change its width and the width is remembered.
  • Folders, with Explorer's own list. The preview hosts a real Explorer browser, so icons, columns, sorting, grouping and the Details / List / Icons view modes are Explorer's. A view dropdown in the header switches between Details, List, Small, Medium, Large and Extra Large icons.
  • A real filter, at the same level. Typing in the filter box shows only the matching direct children of the previewed folder, with their original columns, and clearing it brings the folder back. No subfolder is ever searched.
  • Text and code, detected by content. No extension list: a file is text when its bytes say so, so .ahk, .psd1, .config, extensionless files and anything else just work. UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE and the ANSI code page are decoded, and the footer reports which one was used, the size and the line count.
  • An editor-style toolbar. Word wrap, line numbers (a wrapped continuation keeps its number once), a whitespace inspector that draws spaces as dim dots, and alternating row colors. The four toggles are remembered if you want them remembered, and the defaults are settings.
  • Search inside the file. The same filter box keeps only the matching lines, each with its original line number, and highlights every match with your Windows accent color.
  • Documents without Office. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument files are opened as a zip of XML parts and reduced to their text, so they preview instantly even when Office is not installed. Old binary .doc, .xls and .ppt files use the Windows preview handler when one is registered.
  • Images, video and audio. Images are decoded at full resolution, videos show a frame and audio shows its album art, both through the same still-image providers Windows uses.
  • PDF. Rendered by the Windows PDF preview handler, the same component Explorer's preview pane uses, hosted inside the panel. Zoom and scroll belong to the handler.
  • Archives. A .zip (and any format the shell exposes as a folder) lists its contents in the native list. Formats with no shell namespace fall back to the properties view.
  • A fallback that still helps. Anything else shows the real file icon plus its type, size, modified date and full path.
  • Colors that follow Windows. The panel samples Explorer's actual pixels for the background and the text, and takes the accent from Windows itself, so light, dark and custom accents look native.
  • Explorer never freezes. Listing a folder, reading a file, decoding an image, building a thumbnail or checking a cloud placeholder all run on worker threads. The panel opens at once with a loading state, a new selection cancels the previous load, and a file that is only a cloud placeholder is never downloaded just to be previewed.

A few of the things it previews:

Install

  1. Install Windhawk (Windows 10 or 11).
  2. Open Quick Look on windhawk.net and press Install.
  3. Select a file or folder in File Explorer and press Space.

Quick Look is an injected mod: it runs inside explorer.exe, which is what lets the panel be a real child of the window instead of a window that follows it.

Keys

Key Action
Space Open or close the preview
Esc Close the preview
Click the close button Close the preview with the mouse
Shift + wheel Scroll a text preview sideways when word wrap is off
Mouse wheel / drag the bars Scroll the preview

Settings

Setting Default What it does
Shrink columns to fit the panel On Shrinks the file view and scales the Details columns to the space left by the panel. Turn it off to overlay the panel instead.
Remember the text preview options On Keeps wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots and alternating rows as you left them for the next window or session.
Line numbers by default Off The gutter used when the options are not remembered.
Alternating rows by default Off The alternating row color used when the options are not remembered.

What each file shows

Selection Preview
Folder Explorer's native list, with a view dropdown, a name filter and file/folder counts
Text, code, config, logs Text with wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots, alternating rows and in-file search
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF, OpenDocument The document text, read directly without Office
Old .doc, .xls, .ppt The Windows preview handler when one is installed, otherwise the properties view
Images (png, jpg, gif, bmp, tif, ico, webp…) The decoded image, fitted to the panel
Video and audio A frame or the album art, as Windows produces it
PDF The Windows PDF preview handler, hosted in the panel
Archives (.zip, and formats with a shell namespace) The archive contents in the native list
Anything else The real file icon with type, size, modified date and path

How it behaves

  • The panel never navigates. Double-clicking a folder inside the preview opens its Properties; it does not enter it. Quick Look is a preview, not a file manager.
  • Single click selects. A double click on empty space does nothing.
  • Cloud files are left alone. A file that is only a placeholder is not downloaded to be previewed.
  • Text is capped. A text preview reads the first 200 KB and says so in the footer.

Troubleshooting

  • Space does nothing. The panel only opens when the file list itself has the focus, so a pending rename, an address bar edit or the search box is never hijacked. Click the file list and try again.
  • Something looks wrong. Turn on the Windhawk log for this mod (Advanced tab), reproduce it and attach the log to the issue. It is off by default because it adds a line for every step.
  • A document shows only text. That is by design: modern Office and OpenDocument files are read as text, so layout, images and colors are not part of the preview.

Contributing

Bug reports, fixes and new features are welcome. Open an issue with your Windows build, the mod version, the steps to reproduce it and, when it is visual, a screenshot or a short clip.

For a pull request: fork the repository, branch from main, change quick-look.wh.cpp, confirm it compiles and open the PR describing what changed and why. One bug or feature per PR is much easier to review.

License

Released under the MIT License. See the license file. The inflate code that reads Word and OpenDocument files is derived from zlib's puff.c and keeps its zlib license notice in the source.

Copyright (c) 2026-present David Ravelo.

entry.title: PWA Tray Center 0.5.610
entry.content:
PWA Tray Center

Adds a "Hide to PWA Tray Center" item to the window menu of installed Chrome PWA windows (right-click title bar).

  • Hidden windows keep running (music plays, etc.)
  • One tray icon for all PWAs. By default it stays in the tray. With Always show tray icon turned off (Settings → Advanced), it appears only while PWAs are hidden and disappears when the last one is restored

Tray Icon

  • Left click → opens PWA Tray Center (Fluent flyout, rounded corners, Mica or solid backdrop, chosen in Settings)
  • Right click → menu: Show all / Quit all
  • Center mode (Settings → Panel): Hermes (Quick) closes on a click outside, Titan (Pinned) stays open

Tabs

Tab Description
Media Cards for each Chrome media session: cover, title, artist, PWA source, prev/play-pause/next, draggable progress bar. Right-click for controls. Cover style (small, full or none) and compact view (3 covers per row) are set in Settings.
Apps Hidden PWAs. Left-click to show, right-click for Show/Quit. Badge shows unread counter.
Notifications Toast notifications from Windows notification center. Falls back to unread counter from window title (e.g. (3) Inbox).
Library All installed Chrome PWAs. Left-click to launch/show. Drag to reorder. Right-click for Open/Quit/categories. Search field + category chips for filtering.
Settings All mod options (Panel, Media, PWAs, Notifications, Advanced). No Windhawk settings needed.

Tabs, cards, and tiles are drag-to-reorder; order is remembered.

Notifications are not verified yet and may not work.

Technical Notes

  • Only affects PWA windows (identified by AppUserModelID with _crx_<app id>)
  • Regular browser windows and other programs are untouched
  • Library reads from Chrome's Web Applications folders (default or --user-data-dir)

Chrome Volume

Volume bar in Media tab controls Chrome's system-wide volume (same as Windows volume mixer). Dims when no audio session; changes apply when Chrome starts playing. It can be turned on or off in Settings. The level stays as set after the mod is disabled.

Limitations

  • Does not keep PWA alive after browser process exits
  • Audio may stop if browser freezes or discards background pages (Memory Saver / Efficiency mode)

entry.title: Middle Click Minimize 1.1.3
entry.content:
Middle Click Minimize

This mod allows you to minimize windows by middle-clicking (using the scroll wheel) directly on the title bar.

Exclusions and Conflicts

  • How to exclude programs: To disable the mod for a specific program (e.g., steam.exe or vivaldi.exe), add it to the custom process exclusion list in the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk.
  • Known conflicts: If you use the "Middle-Click New Tab Chrome/Edge/Brave" mod, middle-clicking the empty tab-strip might minimize the browser instead of opening a new tab. You can add your browser to the exclusion list in the Advanced tab to prevent this.

entry.title: Desktop Icons Proximity Reveal 1.0.3
entry.content:
Desktop Icons Proximity Reveal

Hide desktop icons when you are not using them. Hover near an icon or over a custom area to fade them back in.

Features:

  • Draw up to 32 reveal areas around your icons.
  • Reveal each group separately, or show all icons together.
  • Adjust fade speed, hide delay, and hover padding.
  • Preview your areas and save them between sessions.
  • Keep new folders and shortcuts visible while naming them, then hide them after an outside click or a configurable timeout (15 seconds by default).
  • Selected icons stay visible until deselected; press Ctrl+A to reveal all. Disable Keep selected icons visible to turn this off.
  • Keep icons permanently visible using Always-visible icons (whitelist). Enter desktop names separated by semicolons, such as Recycle Bin; Steam; Discord. Names ignore case; * and ? wildcards are supported.

Setup

  1. Enable Show box editor panel in Settings and apply.
  2. Click Edit boxes. All icons appear, including those outside saved areas. Drag around your icons to add areas.
  3. Click Save & apply or Cancel to restore normal hiding. Switch the panel setting off to close it.

The panel stays closed at startup. If its setting is already on, switch it off and on again to reopen it.

Separate groups are enabled by default. Without active areas, hovering near any icon shows all icons. Recycle Bin and folders work too.

How this differs from other mods

Desktop Icon Section Auto-Hide uses a single section or box. This mod adds up to 32 separately animated areas, a drag-to-draw editor, and temporary visibility for newly created items. Flashlight Desktop Icons and Spotlight reveal icons near the cursor rather than inside saved groups. Smooth Desktop Icons Auto-Hide and ZenDesktop focus on hiding and restoring the desktop as a whole.

Note: Requires Windows 10/11 x64. Keep Windows' Show desktop icons enabled. Hidden icons retain their Windows click targets; icons outside all boxes stay hidden unless selected, whitelisted, temporarily revealed, or accessed by keyboard. Redraw areas after changing monitors; avoid running other icon hiding mods.

Rendering hooks adapted from Desktop Icons Transparency by zed712969-crypto.

entry.title: Gradual Night Light 0.4.2
entry.content:
Gradual Night Light

Automatically adjust Windows' native Night light throughout the evening, with an editable daily schedule and optional gradual transitions.

Default schedule

Setting Time Strength
Stage 1 19:00 50
Stage 2 20:00 60
Stage 3 21:00 70
Off time 07:00 Off

Settings

  • Off time: the local time when Night light turns off each day.
  • Stages: add or remove stages with Windhawk's list controls. Each stage has a time and a strength from 1 (weakest) to 100 (warmest). Three stages are provided by default; between 1 and 96 stages are supported.
  • Gradual transitions: interpolate strength between stages. For example, the default schedule produces strength 55 at 19:30. Disable this option to change strength only at each stage's start time.

Times use the local 24-hour HH:MM format. Stages are sorted automatically and the schedule repeats daily, including across midnight. All stage times must be unique and different from Off time. Invalid settings are reported in the mod log; an invalid edit keeps the last valid configuration. If saved settings are invalid at startup, the tool stays running without applying a schedule until valid settings are saved.

Night light switches off at Off time and stays off until the next stage. The last stage holds its strength until Off time. To fade in from almost no warmth, add a stage such as 18:30 with strength 1 before 19:00 with strength 50. Add further stages to create a five-stage schedule or a gradual morning fade.

Behavior and restoration

The scheduler runs in a dedicated Windhawk tool process. Every ten seconds it applies the scheduled temperature directly through Windows' display pipeline. It also checks after display changes, resume, and session unlock.

Settings and Quick Settings show Windows' own Night light configuration. Windows continues running its own schedule in the background. Its transitions can briefly take precedence until the next mod check. The mod pauses while Windows previews its strength slider. Disabling the mod reapplies the temperature requested by Windows' current settings.

The mod reads the current user's Night light settings and state from CloudStore. It applies all scheduled changes at runtime without writing either record. If Windhawk is terminated during a stage, the runtime tint may last until Windows next applies Night light or the user signs out.

If you tested an earlier prerelease, disable it before upgrading so that version can restore the settings it saved.

Requirements and limitations

The mod uses internal Windows Night light display interfaces and the modern CloudStore Current layout. The display driver must support Night light. The tool launcher supports Windhawk 1.7.3 and newer. The runtime interfaces were tested on Windows 11 build 26100, x64, with two displays. HDR and ARM64 have not been verified. If records are missing, open Settings > System > Display > Night light once.

Technical references

The parser and scheduler are independently implemented using the documented research below. No external helper, script, or runtime download is required.

  • Night light registry format research
  • Microsoft Bond CompactBinary protocol
  • Official Windhawk tool mod launcher

entry.title: Floating Taskbar 2.1.13
entry.content:
Floating Taskbar

Left-aligned taskbar layout with the default gradient background.

Features

  • Configure the floating bar width, taskbar area height, bottom gap, and corner radii.
  • Configure the corner radius of taskbar hover highlights.
  • Use the system background, a transparent background, translucent color, a solid color, a linear gradient, or a custom XAML brush.
  • Click through blank areas inside the floating taskbar.
  • Keep tray menus and Quick Settings aligned with the right edge of the bar.

Settings

Widths, area height, spacing, and radii are physical pixels. A taskbar area height of 0 follows the system. A custom XAML background that is left empty also follows the system background.

The same physical-pixel values appear differently at different display scales. Set the values separately if precise consistency across mixed-DPI monitors is required.

Multi-window taskbar highlights are currently detected from the Chinese and English taskbar accessible names. On other Windows display languages, those highlights may not be hidden.

Differences from other mods

Windows 11 Taskbar Styler, Taskbar height and icon size, and MacOS Style Dock can also create a floating or unusually sized taskbar. Floating Taskbar also adds click-through blank space, tray and Quick Settings alignment, automatic tray layout reassertion, and multi-window highlight cleanup. It writes properties on the taskbar's RootGrid and BackgroundFill, so combining it with a Taskbar Styler theme that styles the same properties is not supported.

Use Windhawk's normal mod toggle to disable the mod; there is no separate enable setting.

中文说明

将 Windows 11 任务栏变为独立的悬浮圆角条，可调整长度、区域高度、悬浮间距、 任务栏与待选框圆角，以及背景颜色或渐变。悬浮条内部空白区域可以点击穿透， 托盘菜单与快速设置面板会对齐悬浮条右端。

长度、区域高度、间距和圆角使用物理像素。多窗口任务栏高亮目前依靠中文或英文 辅助功能名称识别，其他显示语言可能不隐藏该高亮。若同时使用 Taskbar Styler 并修改相同的 RootGrid 或 BackgroundFill 属性，两个 Mod 可能冲突。

entry.title: WinPager 0.1.2
entry.content:
WinPager

A virtual desktop pager like KDE Plasma's, living in the Windows 11 taskbar.

  • Shows every virtual desktop with live window outlines, optionally with application icons
  • Click a desktop to switch to it; click the current one to open Task View (configurable)
  • Scroll over it to flip through desktops
  • Drag a window outline onto another desktop to move that window there
  • Hover a desktop for a list of its windows; right-click to add or remove desktops
  • Ctrl+Shift+Win+Left/Right moves the active window to the neighbouring desktop and follows it
  • KWin-style on-screen display when switching, and an option to hide Windows' own "Desktop N" popup
  • A pager on each monitor's taskbar, or one on the main taskbar showing all monitors
  • Can show only a few desktops at a time, scrolling along with the current one
  • Follows light/dark mode and the accent color

The settings mirror those of Plasma's Pager widget, plus position, theme and the switching popups.

The mod runs in its own process; it isn't injected into explorer.exe.

Notes

  • Windows 11 24H2/25H2 (build 26100 and later) only. Like other virtual desktop tools, it relies on undocumented virtual desktop interfaces, so a Windows update can break it. On a build it doesn't know, it shows an error.
  • The taskbar doesn't reserve space for it. Next to a centered row of buttons it shows only as many desktops as fit (at least the current one); on a left-aligned taskbar, a row of buttons long enough to reach the tray runs under it.
  • With "Hide the Windows "Desktop N" popup" on, a volume or brightness popup shown within 0.6 s of a switch is hidden too, since Explorer shows both in the same window.
  • WinPager is also a standalone app, WinPager.exe, built from the same source. Only one of the two runs at a time: if you switch to the mod, quit WinPager.exe and turn off its "Start with Windows".
  • Bugs and ideas: github.com/seanmamasde/WinPager/issues

entry.title: Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation

This mod recreates taskbars inspired by Windows 7, Windows 8 and Windows 8.1 on Windows 10 and 11. The taskbar runs in a dedicated Explorer process on a best-effort basis. Appearance and behavior can vary with the Windows build, DPI, taskbar replacement and other shell mods.

Features

  • Four skin presets: Windows 7, Windows 8 Beta 8148, Windows 8.0 and Windows 8.1, plus Custom for individual Start options.
  • Task buttons, window previews, Jump Lists, notification icons and toolbars.
  • An integrated notification area and taskbar, with a fallback to the native bar if the integrated tray cannot start.
  • Horizontal and vertical layouts, Aero Peek and classic flyout options.
  • Change notification area icon visibility using the Control Panel page that the mod attempts to restore, including on Windows 11; availability and behavior can vary.
  • Static taskbar textures and system colors; the textures do not blur live windows behind the bar. Windows 7 skin adds a cursor-following, icon-colored hover glow for running apps.
  • Local taskbar pins and ordering: the mod does not change Windows pins. Drag to an empty task area to pin; hover a running app to activate its window.
  • An advanced battery flyout option; compatibility may vary between Windows builds.
  • Optional secondary taskbars show pins, windows and the shared private tray. Secondary AppBar registration reserves work area when necessary and allowed by the shell. DPI scaling and flyout positioning are best-effort.
  • Experimental shell minimize-rectangle support supplies reconstructed button coordinates to Windows, without changing Windows 7 Window Animations Restorer. Availability depends on Windows shell-hook delivery and ordering.
  • Optional icon-only horizontal button width: native default, manual logical width, or read-only following of Taskbar height and icon size for standard registry-based Windhawk installations. This does not change icon size or taskbar height and does not hook or modify the other mod. Unsupported installation layouts use the original width.

Themes

Windows 7

Windows 8 Beta 8148

Windows 8.0

Windows 8.1

Custom

Choose individual Start options instead of a preset.

Installation

  1. Install and enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. Choose a skin preset in the mod settings.
  3. Restart the mod after changing settings that require it.

Settings

The mod settings control the skin, Start button, taskbar layout, notification area, previews, flyouts and other behavior. Individual descriptions in Windhawk explain their scope and any restart requirements.

Behavior and limitations

  • The taskbar runs in a separate explorer.exe process on a best-effort basis. Notification-page hooks still run in Explorer, and other Explorer mods can load in the separate process. A watchdog attempts to restore the native taskbar after an unexpected exit; recovery from a hang or other failure is not guaranteed.

  • Skins are approximations; Windows 7 popup frames use the current system's DWM frame when available.

  • The Windows 8 Start corner is illustrated, not a live Start-screen preview.

  • Vertical layout, Aero Peek and classic flyouts may vary between Windows builds.

  • On first use, the mod downloads pnidui.dll, SndVolSSO.dll and batmeter.dll. The advanced battery flyout also downloads stobject.dll and an English or Italian language-pack CAB. Downloaded files are checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes. The Windows 10 1511 stobject.dll is loaded into the dedicated tool process and stays loaded until that process exits.

  • The integrated tray is enabled by default. It creates a private Shell_TrayWnd host and hides the native taskbar. Applications and mods that find the taskbar by class can encounter the private host; tray and AppBar traffic routed to it is processed or forwarded by the mod's UI thread. The host supplies taskbar geometry and forwards wheel input in supported cases, but it does not contain the native taskbar's ReBarWindow32, MSTaskSwWClass, Start button or XAML content. Mods that depend on those windows or content can fail or conflict. Disable the integrated tray and reload the mod if this compatibility trade-off is unsuitable.

  • The integrated tray keeps “Always show all icons” in memory for the current session. It starts from the Windows preference and does not write that preference to the system registry; it is reset when the mod reloads.

  • The Notification Area Icons page uses a private COM provider. The mod attempts to close its hosting window before unloading the Explorer hooks. Behavior has not been verified on every Windows build; if the window cannot be identified or does not respond, close the page before disabling, updating, or reloading the mod.

  • Keep a way to disable the mod or restart Explorer.

  • Windows 11 Taskbar Styler and its skins are technical references; their authors are not involved in this mod.

Credits

  • WinBoeing777 - Testing on Windows 10 22H2 and Suggestions
  • Cips - Testing on Windows 11 25H2
  • Kiyaku - Suggestions and Testing

Disclaimer

This is an independent, unofficial project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed, sponsored or approved by Microsoft Corporation. Windows is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation, used here only to describe the style and compatibility of this mod.

The mod is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, under the GPL-3.0-or-later license. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the author is not responsible for data loss, system instability, blocked updates, or any other damage or consequence arising from the use or misuse of this mod.

Use at your own risk. You are responsible for how you use the mod and for complying with the licenses and terms of any software or resources it interacts with, including Microsoft's terms for any resources downloaded on first use. Keep a way to disable the mod or restart Explorer.

entry.title: Auto-Pause on Disconnect 1.0.0
entry.content:
Auto-Pause on Disconnect

Pauses what you were listening to when the headphones go away: the 3.5 mm cable pulled out, a Bluetooth headset dropped, a USB DAC unplugged. The action lands after Windows has moved the sound back to the built-in speakers, so there is no one-second blast through them.

It does not have to be a pause. The action is a setting, and so is whether it runs on a disconnect, on a connect, or both.

Features

  • Watches the default output device, so wired, Bluetooth and USB removals are caught the same way.
  • Toggle play/pause, mute the output, or unmute it.
  • Waits 300 ms by default before acting, which is enough for Windows to finish moving the stream. Adjustable.
  • Repeats inside one second are folded into a single action. One unplug raises several notifications, and play/pause is a toggle.
  • Only acts while an app is actually playing by default, so it never starts playback on its own.
  • Switching the output by hand is left alone; the old device has to be gone for the action to run.

Settings

  • When a device disconnects and When a device connects pick the direction. Connects are off by default, because plugging headphones in moves the default output too.
  • Audio role to watch is Multimedia by default, or Console, or Both.
  • Action is Toggle play/pause, Mute the default output, or Unmute it.
  • Delay before acting (ms) is how long Windows gets before the action runs, 0 to 3000.
  • Ignore repeats within (ms) is the window used to fold the burst, 0 to 5000.
  • Act only while audio is playing keeps the toggle from starting playback.

Good to know

Play/pause is a toggle, not a pause: if playback was already stopped, it starts again. Leaving Act only while audio is playing on keeps it honest, and the Windows disconnect sound is not counted as playback.

The mute action applies to whichever device is the default after the switch, which is normally the internal speakers. Pair When a device connects with unmute if the headset should bring the sound back when it returns.

The mod runs in a small process of its own rather than inside Explorer, and uses the Windows Core Audio API. The notification callback only wakes a worker thread; the delay, the playback check and the media key all happen there.

entry.title: Explorer Fast Navigation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Fast Navigation

Makes folder navigation faster and less visually disruptive in File Explorer by removing intermediate redraw flicker and deferring toolbar updates until folder contents are loaded.

How it works

In Windows 10 and Windows 11, switching folders triggers intermediate window clearing ("Working on it..." placeholder) and multiple synchronous redraw events from the Ribbon and XAML command bar before files are enumerated.

This mod optimizes the navigation pipeline:

  • Redraw suppression: Suppresses intermediate window clears and synchronous redraw flushes during folder transitions.
  • Deferred toolbar updates: Defers Ribbon and XAML command bar state notifications while files are being enumerated, flushing them once file enumeration completes (DISPID_FILELISTENUMDONE) or batch processing settles.
  • UI freeze reduction: Prevents the UI thread from locking up during folder switches and column grouping changes, lowering CPU repaint spikes.
  • Safety fallback: Incorporates a configurable safety ceiling to ensure pending UI updates always flush even on slow network drives or non-responsive storage.

Observed results

Real-world behavior varies depending on the storage medium and system load:

  • High-speed NVMe drives: Windows virtualizes viewports quickly, but the mod noticeably removes the transient white flicker, suppresses UI repaint churn, and keeps window headers responsive.
  • Mechanical hard drives and laptops: On rotational HDDs or resource-constrained mobile CPUs where disk seek times and background file enumeration can cause visible stalls, the mod eliminates the intermediate "Working on it..." freeze and keeps the Explorer interface smooth during heavy folder browsing and column grouping operations.

Settings

  • Defer immediate navigation paints: Defer immediate activation and layout paints while Explorer switches views.
  • Defer classic ribbon updates: Delay classic ribbon refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer XAML command bar updates: Delay modern command bar refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer navigation bar updates: Delay navigation state updates in classic and modern navigation bars.
  • Safety fallback ceiling (ms): Maximum time (in ms) to wait before forcing a deferred UI update to flush if navigation stalls or on slow storage.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 (21H2, 22H2, 23H2, 24H2)
  • Windows 10 (1809 and later)
  • Architectures: 64-bit (x86-64, ARM64)

Support

If you find this mod useful, you can support its development and maintenance:

  • Support on Buy Me a Coffee

Credits

  • Based on the original implementation by Vivy (@VivyVCCS / enginelesscc).
  • Modernized, refactored, and maintained by gilnett.

entry.title: Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router 2.6.1
entry.content:
🔊 Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router

Volume control for games and setups with several output devices, on Windows 11 and 10: hotkeys for the focused game or app, per-app audio routing, volume locks, Deafen and a replacement volume OSD. Its mixer popup opens on a hotkey on top of any window — including borderless and fullscreen games — without taking the keyboard focus, so games are never minimized. It runs in its own small Windhawk process, not inside Explorer.

✨ Highlights

  • Game hotkeys – change or mute the focused game/app on every device it plays to, without opening anything. UWP apps and protected/elevated games are recognized too.
  • Per-app audio routing – send any app to another output device with the ⇄ button or a right-click.
  • Volume lock – pin the volume of an app or device; a watchdog restores it when a game or Windows changes it. Locks are kept across restarts and marked with a padlock.
  • Deafen background (BETA) – one hotkey mutes or ducks everything except the focused app and your whitelist; pressing it again restores every app individually.
  • Custom volume OSD (BETA) – 9 styles, can replace the Windows volume flyout for the media keys and the volume tooltip of the taskbar, draggable. Like the Windows flyout, it stays while the pointer rests on it, and the mouse wheel or a click on its bar changes the volume.
  • Mixer popup – volume and mute of every app on every output device at once, with live VU meters (up to 60 FPS while open); 17 layouts and 22 color themes.
  • Correct scaling – interface scale 30–300 % multiplied by the Windows display scaling of each monitor; the popup shrinks automatically when it would not fit on the screen.
  • Light on resources – nothing is polled while the popup is closed: the OSD and the volume locks react to Windows audio events, and the keyboard and mouse hooks are installed only while a feature needs them.

🎛️ Mixer layouts

Modern Cards · Compact Strip · Hi-Fi Studio Meters · Fluent Flyout · Cyber Radial HUD · Studio Mixing Desk · Floating Minimal Pill · Cyberpunk Neon Grid · Retro Cassette · LED Meter Bridge · Arcade Panel · Broadcast Console (dual VU) · Control Center Pills · Frosted Glass Tiles · Retro Terminal · Soft Neumorphic · Vertical Channel Strips.

🎨 Themes

Windows 11 Mica · Modern Dark · Light Fluent · AMOLED Black · Frosted Glass · System Accent · Classic Blue · Dracula · Nordic Frost · Cyberpunk Neon · Retro Amber · Tokyo Night · Sunset · Catppuccin Mocha · Forest · Monochrome · Deep Ocean · Rosé Pine · Gruvbox · Solarized Dark · Matrix Green · Midnight Gold.

📺 OSD styles (BETA)

Windows 11 capsule · compact pill · detailed (name, level and device) · circular ring · vertical edge bar · frosted glass · tactical game HUD · stealth dot matrix · Control Center pill.

  • Once the pointer moves onto the OSD, it works like the Windows flyout and stays on screen until the pointer leaves. The mouse wheel or touchpad scrolling over it changes the volume it shows (the master volume or the app), a click or a drag on its bar sets the level, a click on its icon mutes, and a right-click closes it. Otherwise clicks pass through it (unless dragging is enabled), and a hidden pointer (games) is ignored.
  • Replace the Windows volume flyout: the media volume keys and the mouse wheel over the taskbar notification area (tray icons and clock) go through the mod, so Windows doesn't show its own flyout or the Windows 11 volume tooltip. Other volume changes, such as touchpad gestures, headset buttons or laptop hotkey drivers, are made by Windows itself; when Windows shows its flyout for one of them, the mod keeps that flyout invisible (it clips Explorer's indicator window to an empty region and hides it) and shows its own OSD, which follows every step, at 0 % and 100 % too. Only the very first flyout after Explorer starts can show for a moment, before the mod knows its window. Brightness and other Windows indicators use the same window and stay visible: Windows reports brightness changes, so the brightness indicator shows even at 0 % or 100 % volume, except when the brightness itself is already at its limit (then nothing changes and nothing is reported). Airplane mode and other rare indicators shown right after an outside volume change, or at 0 % or 100 %, can be hidden as well. While the option is on, other tray apps and mods that react to the wheel in the notification area (for example Taskbar Volume Control with the tray area as its scroll area) don't get it. Volume indicators of manufacturer utilities (laptop or keyboard software) are separate programs and aren't affected.

⌨️ Hotkeys

Action Default
Open / close mixer Win+Alt+V
Active app volume up / down not assigned
Active app mute / unmute not assigned
Deafen background (when enabled) not assigned
Master volume up / down / mute not assigned

Only the mixer hotkey is set by default, so the mod doesn't take shortcuts that other apps use.

Format: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win + one key (A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, Up, Down, Left, Right, Space, PageUp, PageDown, Num0–Num9, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, Mute…), joined with +. Leave a hotkey empty to disable it. On keyboard layouts with AltGr, Right Alt doesn't count as Ctrl+Alt.

🖱️ Using the mixer

  • Drag a slider or scroll over it to change the volume.
  • Click an app icon to mute or unmute it.
  • Click ⇄ (or right-click a row) to route the app to another device or to lock its volume.
  • Right-click or double-click a device header to make it the Windows default device.
  • Press any key or click outside to close the mixer.

🌐 Language

The mixer, menus and OSD use Language → Mod interface language (automatic, English, Ukrainian, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Russian). The settings page is translated into the same languages and follows the language of Windhawk itself (Windhawk → Settings → Language); other languages show English.

⚠️ Notes

  • Features marked BETA (OSD, Deafen background) are off by default. The mod adds no tray icon: the mixer opens with its hotkey.
  • "Route audio to" uses the same undocumented Windows API as the "App volume and device preferences" page of Windows and EarTrumpet; some apps only switch the device after their audio stream restarts.
  • While a game or app running as administrator is focused, hotkeys work through standard Windows hotkeys: holding volume up/down doesn't repeat there, and Ctrl+Alt combinations don't work there.

🧹 What stays after the mod is disabled

Like the Windows volume mixer, the mod changes Windows' own audio preferences, and Windows keeps them:

  • Output device of an app chosen with "Route audio to": stays until you pick "Windows default device" in the same menu, or use Settings → System → Sound → Volume mixer → Reset.
  • Default output device chosen in the mixer: stays, like a change made in the Windows sound settings.
  • Volume and mute levels of devices and apps: Windows remembers them, as with any mixer.
  • Deafen background: if the mod stops while Deafen is on (crash, shutdown, power loss), it restores the muted and ducked apps the next time it starts.
  • Volume locks are stored by the mod and are no longer enforced while it's disabled.
  • Windows volume flyout (with "Replace the Windows volume flyout"): the mod gives Explorer's indicator window back its normal shape when it's disabled. If its process is killed instead, the Windows flyout stays invisible until Explorer restarts (for example after signing out).

entry.title: Sleep Countdown Reset 1.0.0
entry.content:
Sleep Countdown Reset

Media servers such as Plex keep the PC awake while streaming, but idle time still accumulates. When playback ends and the request is released, Windows checks the expired idle time and sleeps immediately, leaving no time to start the next episode/media/exchange.

This mod hooks the keep-awake APIs inside each server process. Right before the server releases the request, the mod takes over with its own, for a configurable grace period or, by default, the active power plan's sleep timeout. After this period, if playback does not return, the PC sleeps normally.

Display timer and monitor state stay under Windows' control. While the grace period runs, powercfg /requests lists the mod's request under SYSTEM.

Supported servers

Included by default:

  • Plex Media Server
  • Emby Server (EmbyServer.exe)
  • Jellyfin (jellyfin.exe): only with the third-party Prevent Sleep plugin, since Jellyfin alone doesn't keep the PC awake. On PCs with Modern Standby the plugin switches power plans instead, which this mod can't see.

Can be added (see below):

  • Universal Media Server: javaw.exe, with its "Prevent sleep" option set to Playback. That process name is shared by every Java program, so they all get the grace period.
  • qBittorrent (qbittorrent.exe), with "Inhibit system sleep" enabled: grace period after downloads finish.

Not needed: remote desktop and game streaming hosts (Sunshine, Parsec, Steam Remote Play). They forward the remote keyboard and mouse as local input, so Windows already counts the user as present.

Not covered: Windows file sharing (SMB). It runs inside the kernel, with no process to hook.

Adding a program

  1. While the program is serving, run powercfg /requests in a terminal as administrator. The program must be listed under SYSTEM or EXECUTION.
  2. In Windhawk, open this mod's Advanced tab, add the executable name (e.g. qbittorrent.exe) to the custom process inclusion list, and save.
  3. With debug logging enabled, the log should show hooked SetThreadExecutionState for the new process. If the program runs as a Windows service and nothing shows up, check that Windhawk is allowed to inject into services.

Limitation

If the server process exits while holding the request, Windows drops it without any API call, and the mod can't see the release.

entry.title: Mutelith 1.0
entry.content:
Mutelith

Fixes Discord double audio when screen sharing on Windows setups that use virtual audio devices, where viewers hear the game or desktop audio twice, or hear their own microphone coming back with a delay.

Provider Target device (Discord muted)
SteelSeries Sonar SteelSeries Sonar - Microphone
FxSound FxSound Speakers

The provider is detected from the default output device.

While Discord is running, the mod:

  1. Mutes Discord on the provider's target device and on every device outside the provider (speakers, headphones). Only the mute changes, never the volume.
  2. Leaves the provider's other virtual devices alone.
  3. When the mod is disabled, or the default device switches to another provider, unmutes Discord on the devices the rule no longer covers.

With FxSound, FxSound Speakers is usually the only FxSound device, so every other output device is outside the provider and Discord is muted on all of them, voice chat included.

It reacts to Windows audio notifications right away (default device changed, device added or removed, new audio session such as a screen share, a muted session was unmuted) and also checks every 30 seconds.

Windows remembers the mute

The mute is Discord's per-app setting in the Volume Mixer, and Windows saves it for each output device, so it outlives the mod. The mod records each device it muted Discord on and unmutes Discord there once the rule no longer covers it, including after a crash. Windows only lets the mod do that while Discord is running and to have an audio session on that device. If Discord isn't listed for a device in the Volume Mixer when you disable the mod, Discord stays muted there: open the Volume Mixer and unmute Discord, or enable the mod again while Discord is playing audio on that device and switch the default device away from the provider. A mute you set yourself in the Volume Mixer is left alone.

Mutelith app

This is the same rule as the Mutelith app. Use one or the other: while Mutelith.exe is running, the mod does nothing.

Designed and tested for one virtual audio provider at a time.

entry.title: OSD Custom Pill 4.9.11
entry.content:
OSD Custom Pill

An animated on-screen indicator for volume, brightness and virtual desktops on Windows 11.

Volume and brightness

Shows an icon, a progress bar and the current value. The indicator expands when it appears and retracts when it closes.

Elastic deformation

Increasing a value moves and stretches the pill to the right; decreasing it moves the pill to the left. Repeated changes build up the deformation. When you release the key, the pill returns with a spring effect.

The movement, stretching, spring damping and return strength can be adjusted independently in the mod settings.

Compact mode

After several changes in a row, the indicator can become smaller to take up less space. You can choose how many changes activate this mode and when it returns to normal.

Size and position

Adjust the pill's width, height and distance from the bottom of the screen. Opening and closing delays can also be changed.

Virtual desktops

Displays the current virtual desktop name or number when switching desktops. This indicator has its own size, position, animation and duration settings.

Settings

All options are available in Windhawk's Settings tab, with translated labels in supported languages. The main groups are:

Appearance and position — dimensions and screen placement.

Opening and closing — delays and spring response.

Stretching and rebound — movement distance, deformation and elastic return.

Compact mode — activation threshold and return timing.

Virtual desktop indicator — label, dimensions, timing and animation.

Timing values are in milliseconds. Size values are based on 100% display scaling.

entry.title: Explorer Translucent Menus 1.0.2
entry.content:
Explorer Translucent Menus

Apply translucent materials to classic Win32 popup menus in File Explorer. Windows continues to provide menu items, layout, commands, keyboard navigation, and shell extensions. Windows 11's modern context menu is left unchanged.

This is an Explorer-only, menu-focused alternative to the archived TranslucentFlyouts project. It covers classic popup menus hosted by explorer.exe, including desktop and File Explorer context menus. It leaves the main Explorer window background, ordinary controls, and other processes unchanged.

Screenshots

Materials in light and dark themes

Tint and transparency adjustments

Borders and submenus

Requirements

  • Windows 11 22H2 or later (build 22621+), 64-bit.
  • Desktop composition and Windows transparency effects enabled.
  • No other renderer modifying the same Explorer menus.

To open a classic context menu on Windows 11, select Show more options or use Shift+F10. Select Native to disable all hooks. For a temporary bypass, enable Hold Ctrl to bypass in the settings, then hold Ctrl before opening a menu.

Materials

Material Tint opacity
Native No modifications
Solid Always opaque
Transparent Adjustable, no blur
Acrylic Adjustable tint over blur
Modern Acrylic Adjustable tint color, fixed opacity
System Acrylic Fixed Windows recipe
Mica / Mica Alt Fixed Windows recipes

Tint opacity changes the material, not text or icons. Theme selection controls the light or dark palette. Hover highlight opacity can be adjusted separately. Unrecognized saved material values use Acrylic.

Appearance

Enable Hide menu border to suppress the outline on modified menus. This preserves menu dimensions and works with rounded or square corners. Native mode and Ctrl bypass retain the complete Windows appearance. The option also protects the outline setting from later Shell/UxTheme updates while the modified menu is being tracked.

Legacy icon repair converts copied RGB bitmaps to premultiplied alpha. Optional background removal clears only matching corner-connected white, black, or magenta regions. Disable background removal for icons with intentional borders. Transfers that declare per-pixel alpha, and bitmaps with ambiguous partial alpha, retain the original GDI behavior. The mod does not guess whether an existing alpha bitmap is straight or premultiplied.

Scope and rendering approach

This mod keeps the Shell's immersive owner-draw enabled and preserves native menu layout, commands, and shell extensions. Effects are scoped to supported classic popups while a menu is tracked. Preparation validates resources before applying effects and exposes the popup to drawing hooks only after commit. Only successful state changes are recorded for cleanup. Unassociated memory DCs are left to Windows; owner-draw memory DCs require an exact synchronous WM_DRAWITEM match. GDI and UxTheme hooks are installed in Explorer, but forward to Windows outside a tracked menu. The scope is the popup effect, rather than a replacement for Explorer's overall interface rendering.

Translucent Windows and Win32 UI Modernizer already offer translucent classic menus. Translucent Windows shares background-effect configuration between windows and flyouts, with menu drawing integrated into its broader theme-rendering path. Win32 UI Modernizer lets users disable its Explorer section and other general features, but its modern menu modes disable immersive owner-draw and also modernize ComboBox dropdowns.

The purpose of this separate implementation is to provide a dedicated popup renderer that retains the Shell's owner-draw path and can accompany a separate Explorer background renderer. Restricting process targets or adding material presets alone does not provide that rendering behavior. An equivalent mode in a broader UI mod would need to isolate menu rendering and preserve immersive owner-draw as well.

Compatibility

Menu effects from these mods conflict when enabled on the same Explorer popups:

  • Translucent Windows: Flyout effects also renders classic menus, dropdowns, and tooltips. Disable that option to remove its flyout effects.
  • Win32 UI Modernizer: set Menus and dropdowns to Native (no modernization). Both modern modes apply their own acrylic rendering and disable immersive owner-draw.

These settings turn off their direct menu features. Their remaining Explorer effects and shared drawing hooks depend on other settings, so compatibility must be evaluated with the configuration in use. To avoid their remaining hooks in Explorer while continuing to use them in other applications, exclude explorer.exe from their targets in Windhawk's Advanced tab.

This mod is also compatible with ExplorerBlurMica, which supplies the main Explorer window backdrop. This mod keeps its effects confined to classic popup menus and leaves the main window backdrop to ExplorerBlurMica.

Unknown owner-drawn menus, custom background brushes, high contrast, remote sessions, disabled transparency, and recognized conflicting renderers are left unchanged. Settings changes reload the mod. Menu opening animations follow the Windows settings and the caller's flags, including when effects are active.

Menus whose previous system-backdrop value cannot be read stay native. Unreadable optional dark-mode and corner preferences are left unchanged. Recorded values are restored on live-window cleanup; failed restores remain pending for retry. There are no public getters for prior blur regions or extended-frame margins, and the Accent getter is unavailable on some builds. Cleanup of those states is best-effort, not a lossless restoration guarantee for an unknown renderer. A missing border-color snapshot likewise uses the Windows default on cleanup. Destroyed popup HWNDs release their window-owned effects without extra resets.

The implementation uses version-dependent Windows interfaces: the composition attribute exports, UxTheme ordinal 74, the DarkMode::Menu theme, menu layout message 0x1e2, and Shell window properties. It does not read private Shell item structures, patch instructions, download symbols, or replace the menu loop.

Troubleshooting

Enable log output in Windhawk's Advanced tab to record menu preparation, material and border application results, native fallback reasons, and cleanup. There is no separate logging setting in this mod. Native mode registers no menu hooks, so it reports initialization rather than individual menu openings.

Credits and license

Informed by TranslucentFlyouts, Translucent Windows, and Custom Cached Context Menu. This implementation is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later.

entry.title: Mac OS 27 Finder Bar 1.0.0
entry.content:
Mac OS 27 Finder Bar

A Windhawk mod that adds a macOS 27-style menu bar to the top of the screen in Windows 11: the menus of the app in front on the left, and system status, Control Center, notifications and the clock on the right, all in live glass.

Available in English, Português, Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano and 中文（简体）. The language follows Windows automatically, or can be picked in the settings.

Left side

  • Logo menu: About This PC, System Settings, Microsoft Store (both with pending update counts), Force Quit, Show Desktop, Sleep, Hibernate, Restart, Shut Down, Lock Screen, Sign Out and Menu Bar Settings…
  • Active app name (shown as Finder for the desktop and File Explorer, a name you can change): hide the app, hide others, open file location, close window, quit, force quit
  • Global menu:
    • apps with a classic menu bar (Win32): the app's real menus
    • modern apps: the app's menu bar read through UI Automation when it exists
    • browsers, File Explorer, Office, VS Code and other apps: ready-made menus that send the app's own keyboard shortcuts
    • a Window menu with the app's open windows
  • Help menu with a search across all the app's menus; ← → move between menus (optional Ctrl+F2 opens the bar from the keyboard)

Right side

  • Display: dark mode, night light, projection modes
  • Keyboard layout (when there is more than one), emoji, on-screen keyboard
  • Battery (percentage, charging, time remaining), Wi-Fi (current network, available and known networks), Bluetooth and Sound (scroll on the icon to change the volume, right-click to mute, switch output and input)
  • Now Playing: the song name scrolls across the bar when it doesn't fit; the panel has a large-cover or compact layout and a progress bar drawn as a line, a colored line or a wave
  • Focus (when Do Not Disturb is on), Search (Windows Search or Siri Plus Launchpad), microphone and camera (the icons turn orange and green while an app uses them, as on the Mac; click to see which apps use them and mute the microphone), Weather (Open-Meteo, MET Norway or wttr.in, no account needed) and the Notifications button
  • Clock: the calendar and your agenda from your own .ics files, imported right from the settings window. Date and time formats are configurable
  • An arrow collapses the icons that don't fit; each icon can be turned on or off in the settings

Control Center

Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, media playing, dark mode, Do Not Disturb, brightness, sound and audio output, plus tiles you can add: night light, airplane mode, screenshot, screen recording, power mode, energy saver (one click turns it on and off), magnifier, lock screen, calculator, Task Manager, emoji and show desktop.

  • Edit Controls lets you add, remove, move and resize tiles
  • Clicking power mode opens a box under Edit Controls, as wide as the panel, with the Windows 11 power modes and power plans (repeated plans are hidden)
  • Tile names that don't fit scroll when the mouse is over the tile
  • Tiles can be pills or rounded squares; a tile that is on shows a colored circle or turns into a whole white pill
  • Optional: blur and dim the screen while the Control Center is open; cascade or fade animation when it opens

Notice pills

Small glass pills drop from the bar for headphones, audio output, low battery, charger, Focus, Caps Lock, USB devices and drives, finished downloads, copy and cut, screenshots and screen recordings. Pills you can act on (open and edit a screenshot or recording, open a download, reply to a message) stay 2.5 times longer and are kept in the bell panel; the rest only show in the pill. Volume, brightness and Bluetooth changes can show as floating pills too. The pill's style (glass, liquid glass or dark), size, position, duration and opening and closing animations are all configurable.

Notifications

Turn on Windows notifications in logo → Menu Bar Settings… → Notice pills (off by default) and the bar shows your apps' notifications:

  • in the pill and in the bell panel, grouped by app
  • reply to messages (like WhatsApp) right from the pill, when the app supports replies
  • drag a notification aside in the panel to clear it
  • Only the bar shows notifications: optional; Windows' own banners move off the screen while the bar shows them, and come back when the option or the mod is turned off

Bar and glass

  • Bar background: fully transparent (default), Windows blur glass, or liquid glass (experimental); opaque when the active app is maximized (optional)
  • Live glass: panels blur what's behind them in real time, with an experimental liquid glass with edge refraction (on by default)
  • Menus use their own frosted glass (with a transparency slider) or the same glass as the Control Center
  • Light, dark or automatic theme, nine selection colors for the bar and menus, font, font size, icon size and bar height
  • Hides with full-screen apps, can hide automatically until the mouse touches the top, and shows on every monitor (each optional)

Settings

Logo → Menu Bar Settings… opens a window in the same style as Siri Plus Launchpad: sections on the left with search, every setting applied live without restarting the bar. It's the only place for those settings. Windhawk's settings page has the few the window doesn't: font, glass tints, theme, the name shown for the desktop, ready-made menus, Control Center tile look, opening animation, tray click, the app update count and .ics file paths, plus Reset the bar's settings, which puts the window's options back to their defaults if the bar ever doesn't show up.

What changes Windows settings

Some Control Center tiles and menu items change real Windows settings, the same ones Windows' own quick settings change. They stay changed after the mod is turned off, as they would if you used Windows' quick settings:

  • Dark mode: the app and system light/dark theme (sets both to the same value)
  • Night light: on or off
  • Power mode and power plan: picking a power mode also switches the plan to Balanced, as Windows requires
  • Energy saver and Do Not Disturb
  • Brightness, default audio device, volume and mute, microphone mute, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios, Wi-Fi network and display mode (projection)

Nothing is changed unless you click the matching tile or item.

Network use

The mod only goes online for features you set up yourself (the calendar reads local .ics files only, never the network):

  • Weather, once you pick a place: the place search uses OpenStreetMap Nominatim or Open-Meteo, and the forecast comes from the service you choose (Open-Meteo, MET Norway or wttr.in) with the place's coordinates rounded to about 1 km. Turning the weather icon off stops all requests.
  • App update count (off by default, in Windhawk's settings): runs winget upgrade, which checks winget's sources online. The mod doesn't accept winget's source agreements for you. The Windows Update count is offline.

Privacy

The copy pill only says "Copied" or "Cut": it never shows what was copied, and it skips anything an app marks as private (password managers do), the same way Windows' clipboard history does.

How it runs

The bar runs in its own Windhawk process (shown as Windhawk in Task Manager), so if it ever fails, the taskbar and desktop keep working. Explorer keeps only a small hook that copies the tray icons' registrations to the bar. If that process is ended by hand, turn the mod off and on again in Windhawk to bring the bar back.

Known limitations

  • Apps without a classic menu bar use ready-made menus based on keyboard shortcuts.
  • Bluetooth lists classic (non-BLE) devices and opens Settings to connect and disconnect.
  • Power mode and energy saver use undocumented Windows functions; if Windows refuses, the tile opens the matching Settings page.
  • Screen recording uses Win+Shift+R and needs an up-to-date Snipping Tool.
  • Replying from the pill works with apps that register a notification activator with Windows; otherwise the pill opens the app and copies your text.
  • With live glass (and the bar's liquid background), the bar and panels don't show up in screenshots.
  • If Windhawk itself runs as administrator (portable mode started elevated), the bar doesn't show the tray icons: letting the shell's tray data reach an elevated bar would also let any app send it fake icons.

entry.title: Adobe Dark Menus 1.0.0
entry.content:
Adobe Dark Menus

This Windhawk mod gives Adobe apps on Windows dark menus: real menu bars, top-bar dropdowns, context menus and dropdown lists. It also colors their standard title bars to match.

Everything happens inside each app's own process. No system colors are changed and no other application is affected.

Supported apps

Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Dreamweaver, After Effects, Premiere Pro, Audition, Media Encoder, Bridge and Acrobat.

Screenshots

Photoshop: a dropdown list in the options bar

Illustrator: a context menu

InDesign: the Type menu

After Effects: the Window menu, with the menu bar and title bar

After Effects: the blend modes on a timeline layer

Premiere Pro: a context menu on a timeline clip

Premiere Pro: the Sequence menu, with the menu bar and title bar

Related mods

These overlap with this mod. Running them together in the same app has not been tested, so use one or the other for the apps above.

  • Photoshop Dark Menus covers Photoshop only. This mod does everything it did and reaches the other Adobe apps, so disable it if you use this one.
  • Dark mode context menus darkens the menus Windows draws, in every app and in fixed colors. It does not reach menus an app draws itself, which is why Photoshop stays light with it, or dropdown lists. This mod uses the same technique for the menus Windows draws, so exclude the Adobe apps from it in its Advanced tab.
  • After Effects Theme and Premiere Pro Theme recolor the whole interface of those two apps in palettes of their own, title bar, menu bar and menus included. They answer the same menu bar messages as this mod, so if you use one of them, exclude that app from this mod in its Advanced tab.
  • Windows 11 Custom Title Bar Colours and Auto Custom Titlebar Colors color title bars in every app. If you prefer one of them, turn off Dark Title Bars here.

Options

  • Menu Background Color: Background color (Default: #2D2D2D).
  • Menu Text Color: Text color for active items (Default: #DCDCDC).
  • Highlight Background Color: Color when hovering over an item (Default: #505050).
  • Highlight Text Color: Text color when hovering over an item (Default: #FFFFFF).
  • Separator Line Color: Color for separator lines. Set to match the background color to hide them completely (Default: #383838).
  • Disabled Text Color: Text color for disabled menu items (Default: #808080).
  • Border Color: Color of the frame around menus an app draws itself and around dropdown lists. Leave empty to keep the system frame on those menus and to use the background color on lists (Default: #2D2D2D).
  • Theme Dropdown Lists: Darken the dropdown lists an app draws itself, using the colors above (Default: on).
  • Darken Menus Windows Draws: Use Windows' dark menu theme, and paint real menu bars dark (Default: on).
  • Dark Title Bars: Color standard title bars to match the menus (Default: on).
  • Title Bar Color: Leave empty to match Menu Background Color (Default: empty).
  • Title Bar Text Color: Leave empty to let Windows choose, which dims the text on a window that is not active (Default: empty).

Colors can be given as #RRGGBB or the short #RGB form.

The colors apply to real menu bars, to menus an app draws itself (Photoshop's) and to dropdown lists. Menus Windows draws itself keep Windows' own dark colors.

How it works

Adobe's apps do not all draw their menus the same way, and sharing a library does not settle it: Illustrator and InDesign ship the same AdobeOwl.dll as Photoshop, yet Windows draws their menus and Photoshop draws its own. So the mod decides menu by menu, by whether the items are owner-drawn (MFT_OWNERDRAW).

Menus Windows draws

This is most menus in most Adobe apps. Windows paints them through its theme engine, and uxtheme has a dark variant of that drawing which is off unless a process asks for it. The mod asks for it with SetPreferredAppMode(ForceDark) and FlushMenuThemes, and puts the process back when it is disabled. This technique comes from Dark mode context menus by MGGSK, and needs Windows 10 1903 or later.

Real menu bars

Some apps, After Effects for one, have a real Win32 menu bar. The dark theme does not reach it, but Windows offers it to the window first through the undocumented WM_UAHDRAWMENU and WM_UAHDRAWMENUITEM messages, so the mod paints it from a DefWindowProc hook, in the colors above. Those messages were worked out in win32-custom-menubar-aero-theme.

Menus an app draws itself

Photoshop owner-draws its menu items with plain GDI, so the theme has nothing to attach to. Measured in Photoshop, the popups go up via TrackPopupMenuEx and each item is painted with:

  • FillRect(hdc, &rc, (HBRUSH)(COLOR_MENU + 1)) for the item background, and (HBRUSH)(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT + 1) for the hovered item. These system color pseudo-handles are resolved inside user32 from shared memory, so they bypass GetSysColor and GetSysColorBrush hooks entirely.
  • GetSysColor(COLOR_MENUTEXT / COLOR_GRAYTEXT / COLOR_HIGHLIGHTTEXT) for text.
  • Its own 1px FillRect for separator lines.

So every pixel of a menu item is reachable from inside the process:

  • FillRect / PatBlt are hooked and, while a menu item is being painted, sys-color pseudo-handles are re-resolved through this mod's own color table, and 1px fills inside a menu DC are recolored to the separator color.
  • GetSysColor / GetSysColorBrush are hooked for the menu color indices, but only while a menu item is actually being painted, that is, inside a WM_DRAWITEM of type ODT_MENU, so the app's dialogs and panels keep the system colors. "While a menu is open" would be far too broad: a menu runs a modal message loop that keeps dispatching to every other window on the thread, and an unrelated repaint would pick the menu colors up.
  • MENUINFO::hbrBack is stamped on each owner-drawn popup at WM_INITMENUPOPUP, covering the popup background that the system paints around the items. It is never stamped on a menu Windows draws, where it would put a custom background behind a theme's gutter, separators and text.
  • The popup's non-client frame is drawn kernel-side, where no user-mode hook can reach it. So the popup is subclassed at creation and the frame is repainted with the border color after it.

Dropdown lists

The dropdown lists are stock Win32 combo boxes whose list is the system's own ComboLBox window. Photoshop owner-draws the rows but takes their colors from the system, and not consistently: one list reads COLOR_WINDOWTEXT for its row text where another reads COLOR_MENUTEXT, and one fills its rows from a color it asks for where another fills them with a (HBRUSH)(COLOR_X + 1) pseudo-handle. Both routes are therefore covered, over a table that maps every background index to the background color and every text index to the text color. The list window is subclassed so that all of it applies only while that list or one of its rows is painting, which leaves every other control reading those same colors alone, including anything the app repaints in response to a selection.

A list whose rows Windows draws is left alone, the same rule as for menus. Windows fills it from a brush no hook can reach, so recoloring the text alone would leave light text on white. So is a list that stays open inside a dialog, such as the ones in the font picker, since it is part of the dialog rather than a dropdown.

Scroll arrows

A menu too tall for the screen gets scroll arrows, which the Windows kernel draws directly in light colors, below anything the dark theme or a hook can reach. So the mod paints over them straight afterward, turning the light square dark and the dark triangle light. A disabled arrow stays dimmer, since this inverts what is there rather than drawing a new one. On a menu an app draws itself, Windows draws a bare triangle instead of the square, and the mod recolors it to Menu Text Color or Disabled Text Color.

Title bars

Windows 11 lets a process color a standard title bar through DwmSetWindowAttribute, so nothing is drawn here: the mod sets DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE and DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR on each top-level window with a caption, and puts them back when it is disabled. On Windows 10 2004 or later the dark flag still gives a dark title bar, without the custom color.

A window that draws its own title bar, such as the main window of Photoshop, Illustrator or InDesign, is left alone. This is checked per window, so the dialogs in those apps are still colored. The dialog's contents stay whatever color the app or Windows paints them.

Scope

Anything an app paints from its own palette rather than from a system color or the theme is out of reach, such as Photoshop's font browser and the Glyphs panel's character cells. Recoloring those would mean matching color values rather than intercepting a system one, in windows where a light fill can be the content.

A dropdown list Windows draws itself keeps its normal colors, as described above.

Long menus scroll rather than splitting into columns, because Windows turns its theme off for any menu that has columns, which leaves them light.

Source and bug reports

The mod is developed at github.com/sabergraphics/adobe-dark-menus.

Report a problem in Issues. Menu drawing depends on the environment more than most things do, so please say which Adobe app and version and which Windows version you are on, what your display scaling is, and which menu or dropdown list is wrong. A screenshot usually says more than a description does.

entry.title: Unlock "Folder In Use" 1.0.0
entry.content:
Unlock "Folder In Use"

When Explorer refuses to delete, move or rename something because it is in use ("Folder In Use" / "File In Use"), this mod finds out which processes are blocking it and lets you decide what to do.

When the warning appears, a small dialog lists the blocking processes and offers:

  • End processes and continue - terminates the processes and presses Try Again for you, so Explorer completes the original operation.
  • Only end processes - terminates the processes and leaves Explorer's warning open so you can retry yourself.
  • Cancel - does nothing.

If Explorer windows are open inside the item being processed, they are moved up one level.

How it works

  • The mod runs as a tool in its own dedicated process, not inside Explorer, so a problem in it can't affect the taskbar or the desktop.
  • The warning is detected through its internal UI Automation identifiers instead of its text, so it works with any display language.
  • The blocked item is identified from the name shown in the warning. Only the text elements of the interrupt panel itself are read (starting from the Try Again button), never the rest of the progress window, and names are compared in full. Only the selected items (or entries inside selected folders) whose name matches exactly are scanned.
  • The matched paths are listed in the details of the prompt, so you can see what was scanned before ending anything.
  • Blockers are found with the Restart Manager, the current directory of each process, and the system handle table. Every Explorer process is excluded.
  • Processes are opened while scanning and terminated through those same handles, so a process that exits and whose PID is reused is never terminated by mistake.

Notes

  • Ending a process terminates it immediately. Unsaved work in that process is lost.
  • Elevated or protected processes can't be ended from this mod.
  • If the item named in the warning can't be matched with the selection, the mod says so and does nothing.
  • The mod relies on internal details of Explorer's operation dialog, which may change in future Windows versions.

Settings

  • Modern dialogs - use task-dialog style windows instead of classic message boxes.
  • Show message when nothing is found - show a dialog when the blocked item or its blocking process could not be identified (enabled by default).
